title: 4.8 ELECTRICITY STORAGE
summary: Storage as Price Arbitrage: Rethinking Grid-Scale Electricity Storage — this chapter builds from the basic economic premise (storing cheap off-peak power to sell during expensive peak periods) through the physical technologies that can do it (pumped hydro, compressed air, flywheels, and batteries, including electric vehicles as a distributed battery source), and finally into how to value such assets. It emphasizes that valuation is not one-size-fits-all: approaches like the off-peak/peak price ratio, treating nightly purchases as a futures series, or seasonal pumped-hydro arbitrage all depend on the facility's actual operating profile, while round-trip efficiency losses set a floor on the price spread needed to break even. The chapter also flags the practical limits of this opportunity — operational and environmental risks that deter investors (particularly in pumped hydro) and the self-defeating dynamic where widespread storage adoption narrows the very price spread that made it profitable.
